title: Uroboros: Deadly Poison
paragraphs: “Send the Magic Corps immediately! Cast the Judgment spell! Hurry!”
The queen says this in a desperate tone.
“What on earth is that?”
“Heroes, please be careful! That’s a monster that infects living creatures and grows rapidly! You must not touch it under any circumstances!”

It seems to have turned into a truly terrifying monster. The situation resembles the magical hazard that occurred during the loop when we went to Faubrey before, but it’s progressing far more rapidly than that.
“It looked like that woman…”
“Lord Iwatani, please be careful as well! Even for a hero, there’s no guarantee you can survive the corruption of an Apostle of Ouroboros!”
“It’s revealed its true form, hasn’t it!”
Fleon-chan’s feathers bristled as she said,
“No, that’s not it. But if we don’t eliminate it as soon as possible, the number of victims will only keep rising.”
“That’s… that’s Malty, isn’t it!”
“You know it too! Just hurry up! Before it’s too late!”
They seem to be in a bit of a bind.
“I suppose I have no choice. It’s the least I can do out of compassion for a former comrade. Rest in peace!”

Crimson Swine, I’m surprised your true identity was revealed right here. Still, you offered a parting gift of words that would rot in your mouth. I’ll cast Magic to burn away the countless vines reaching out at me.
“Liberation Flame Floor X!”

With a crackle, I’ll scorch every single one of the Ouroboros Apostles I’ve targeted with Magic flames. Oh? Judging by the resistance, their magical defense seems quite high. Even though I’m burning them, they’re still moving. They’re trying to escape the flames! To survive a “Liberation” Magic spell—and a X-rank one at that—is… quite tenacious. Well, I guess I have no choice!
“Brionac X!”
I’ll deliver the final blow with a sweeping Brionac strike. And just like that, we’ve completely eradicated the mutated monster—the Crimson Swine, an Apostle of Ouroboros.
“Looks like we took care of it pretty easily…”
“Maltyiiiiii!”
That Trash is screaming his head off, but his eyes are vacant.
“This can’t be! It mustn’t be! Malty, why you of all people! Aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaahhhhhhhhhhh!?”
The extent of his panic is unlike anything we’ve seen before. It’s quite different from what I expected, but he’s taken a serious hit.
In other words, it’s this. I’ve finally gotten my revenge here for what I couldn’t do back at Shieldfreeden.
“Mother…”
At this point, the Finacée addresses the Queen and stares at Trash.
“You seem quite flustered. What happened?”
“No… At first, it was supposed to be nothing more than a matter of dealing with a family disgrace before it became public…”

The queen explained that Trash and Crimson Swine had pretended to be remorseful, but she’d caught them red-handed poisoning her Father’s plate—and she’d decided to settle the matter by making them taste the very poison she’d taken herself.

“So, I don’t know what kind of poison it was, but are you saying that Bitch tried to slip me some incredibly potent poison? And Trash—it turns out it was a laxative… but it doesn’t look like he’s about to wet himself or anything.”

Father, his face pale, is staring at the spot where Crimson Swine used to be and at Trash, who looks completely dazed. Even though Trash drank a powerful laxative, he looks like that’s the least of his worries.
“Sister… how foolish. But so such a poison does exist, then?”
“Yes… that’s right. Melty, this is something I hadn’t told you before, but we have a history with this poison.”
“Huh?”

“The poison that child used is likely the Ouroboros Venom. It’s a forbidden poison—one so dreaded that even Zeltoble is said to have erased the formula from existence, and whose very name we hesitate to pass down to future generations.”
It seems the Queen knows about this deadly poison.
“Such a poison… what does it have to do with us?”
“Melty, there was something I once told you while omitting part of the story—the story of your late brother.”

Huh? I feel like I’ve heard that somewhere before. Oh, right—I heard a similar story in a previous loop. If I recall correctly, her Finacée’s brother was poisoned to death, and Trash came to harbor a deep grudge against Siltvelt.
“I do recall hearing that he was poisoned… but surely not!”

“Yes, it is exactly that. While this has no direct connection to Lord Iwatani, it occurred in the past, while Melromarc was in the midst of trying to build friendly relations with Siltvelt… It was an incident that caused Aultcray’s hatred toward Siltvelt and the Demi-Humans to intensify even further…”
And so, the queen began to recount the events of the past.

That incident refers to the story of the prince who was caught between the Crimson Swine and my Finacée—a story my Finacée told me during the loop where I remained in Melromarc. Based on that story, I told my Father and the others about Fleon-chan, and they explained to me that Fleon-chan had been killed by the Crimson Swine.

Well, let’s set aside that preamble—or rather, my personal circumstances—for now and focus on the Queen’s story. Apparently, it concerns the Crimson Swine’s younger brother—the prince of Melromarc—whom the Queen had told her Finacée about. As a premise, I explained to my Father that Siltvelt and Melromarc had been enemies for a long time. Of course, this was from Melromarc’s perspective regarding the country of Siltvelt.

“Aultcray… no, I called him by that name just now, didn’t I? Trash was once known as the Wise King; he was a brilliant strategist and hero who saved Melromarc when it was on the verge of being conquered and destroyed by Siltvelt.”
“This guy?”
My father is looking at Trash as if he simply cannot believe it from the bottom of his heart.
“I won’t deny that there’s not a trace of that left now. But please understand first that it is a fact.”
“Yeah, yeah. So?”
“Thanks to Trash, Tyran-Fayon, the leader of Siltvelt at the time, was defeated and forced to retreat. That is how peace came to Melromarc. Because of that achievement, Trash became my husband, but…”
The queen paused for a moment before continuing her explanation to her fathers and the others.

“And so, finally, the extremists in Siltvelt began to lose their power, while the pro-peace faction gained strength. Both sides made concessions to the point where they were seeking to build friendly relations with Melromarc, fulfilling each other’s demands as they worked toward a lasting peace.”
“But…” the Queen said, glancing at Trash as she covered her mouth with her fan. “That’s when the prince was assassinated, isn’t it?”
“An envoy of peace from Siltvelt poisoned our prince, Ciser, right in front of Trash during a banquet.”
That’s the part of the story I heard in the previous loop.
“Mother… judging by Father’s condition…”

“Yes… The poison used on that occasion was a substance known as the ‘Uroboros Venom.’ Just like the Bitch earlier, Sizer’s corpse—killed by the poison—transformed, along with his soul, into a monster known as an ‘Apostle of Uroboros.’ It began to expand its influence by drawing in surrounding living creatures and attempting to contaminate the area.”

Hmm… So it seems something like that did indeed happen in Melromarc. I’ve been through countless loops, but this is the first I’ve heard of it. However… I seem to recall it bearing a strong resemblance to a phenomenon known as a “magical hazard,” caused by the Homunculus Research Institute—or was it the “White-Coated Pigs”? In the sense that it’s a conceivable catastrophe, I suppose they’re the same.

“After expanding its influence to a certain extent, it creates monsters within that sphere to further expand its power… The records of the Four Holy Heroes’ past battles describe it as such a monster. It’s enough for you to consider it a threat of that magnitude.”
“I see… So it sounds like the Bitch was carrying some incredibly potent poison.”
“How did you handle it back then? To be honest, it was a pretty tough monster.”
“And you’re the one saying that—the guy who incinerated it in an instant, wiping it out without a trace?”

“Well, to me, it wasn’t even as much of a threat as a mosquito. But its durability was quite high. If I hadn’t properly enhanced myself, it wouldn’t have been just a tough fight—it would’ve been much worse.”

“……I suppose you and the others don’t know this, Lord Iwatani, but Trash was one of the ‘Seven Star Heroes of the Staff’—a hero wielding a weapon distinct from the Four Holy Weapons. At the time, Trash was deeply torn, but he wielded his staff and, working in coordination with the nation’s Magic Corps, unleashed layer upon layer of Ceremonial Magic to somehow eradicate them. It was fortunate that the casualties were kept to a minimum.”
“But…” the Queen said, casting a pitying glance toward Trash. I see. Given those circumstances, it makes sense that he harbors such intense hatred toward Siltvelt.
“A Seven-Star Hero, huh… Well then, why don’t you become a hero and save the world from the Wave?”

“I’d like to ask you to keep this confidential, but because of the events of that time, Trash’s hatred toward Siltvelt grew even stronger, and his thinking became increasingly rigid… Perhaps the Seven Star Weapons of the Staff, seeing Trash consumed by such a thirst for revenge, gave up on him and vanished. This is something we cannot reveal to other nations. If it gets out, it’ll lead to war, so everyone, please be very careful.”
The Queen is emphasizing this to us.
“We must not engage in meaningless conflict!”
At this point, Fleon-chan steps forward and makes her case. That’s right. I think she’s absolutely right.
“War is out of the question. Let’s keep this a secret!”
“I don’t know why you’re the one calling the shots here… but let’s continue. I get that the use of that poison triggered Trash’s trauma… but isn’t it a bit strange for him to be this flustered?”

“Yes, if that were all there was to it, it would have been fine. But Bitch has exhibited countless suspicious behaviors regarding past incidents as well. Technically, the culprit—a member of the Siltvelt—confessed… but it was that girl who uncovered the truth.”
“Bitch’s testimony? That’s way too suspicious.”

“Technically, when you weigh all the various testimonies together, it was thought unlikely that that girl was among the perpetrators. However… I can’t help but feel there might be another truth behind this—it was, after all, a truly abhorrent incident.”
I see, so that’s what happened. I’m sure Crimson Swine is the culprit. I just don’t know what kind of scheme he used.
You can probably figure out the rest. With that, the Queen placed her hand on Trash’s shoulder and said,
“Trash, it seems that girl was the one who killed Sizer.”
“――!! Aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!?”
Trash clutched his head, crouched down, and let out a bloodcurdling scream. This has turned out to be quite a strange outcome.
“Bub!”
Soon after, Shadow Pig came running up to the Queen, holding some sort of bottle. That bottle… looks a lot like a bottle of Uroboros poison.
“It looks like it’s empty. It seems to have evaporated… So there was a hidden cupboard in part of the wall in that girl’s room, wasn’t there?”
Huh? That’s strange, isn’t it? I should’ve stored the Uroboros poison I laced into the spear to destroy the evidence. There’s absolutely no way the evidence should have surfaced…
“So, that Bitch—cornered by me—tried to poison me with her secret stash of poison, only to end up drinking it herself. She’s got exactly what she deserved.”
“Yes… she really was a foolish girl who needed to be dealt with.”

Just as I thought the Trash had stopped crying, he stood up listlessly—looking every bit like a frail old man, devoid of any fighting spirit—and began to stagger off. Where on earth does he think he’s going?
“…Make sure to secure the Trash and keep him under guard in the appropriate room…”
Following the Queen’s orders, Trash was led away by the soldiers. His face looked more aged than I’d ever seen it before.
“Analyze the contents of this bottle. But since it’s such a loathsome substance, investigate it with the utmost care.”

The Ouroboros poison I used is gone. But the fact that another vial has appeared… the darkness of the Crimson Swine is truly horrifying. Still, considering what happened in the first world, the contents of that vial were likely already gone. The poison intended for my Father was mild enough that, if treated promptly, he could have been saved—it was the sort of poison that would have required transport to a clinic.
“Ah… aaaah…”

Huh? When I looked behind me, the Immortal was watching the unfolding events with a speechless expression. We did it! An eye for an eye! A tooth for a tooth! Or so I thought, but the Immortal looked as if he couldn’t believe what was happening.
“W-Wait, Spear Hero, y-you surely couldn’t have…!”
Oh, so he’s figured out the truth! That’s right! It’s a fitting poison for the Crimson Swine who poisoned Fleon! Yeah! That’s right!
“…Fleon, this place is dangerous. You’d better leave this place quickly.”
“Oh? Sage, what’s the matter?”
“It’s not a matter of ‘what’s the matter’…”
The sage is glaring at me.
“Spear Hero, it seems entrusting Fleon to you was a mistake.”
“What do you mean by that?”
Did I do something wrong? I have absolutely no recollection of doing anything to betray the Immortal’s trust.
“Don’t you understand? What you did is not something one can do with a clear conscience!”
Oh, it seems the Immortal simply cannot forgive me for being the one who poisoned the Crimson Swine. This is a difference in perspective.

From my perspective, Fleon—my very first and most important Filolial-sama—was killed by the Crimson Swine, so this is simply revenge. But this Immortal seems to think Fleon is, by some stroke of luck, still alive. I’ve been commanded by Filo-tan to live with integrity. I show no mercy to evil. I honestly channeled my anger and made him pay.
But the Immortal isn’t convinced. Well then… there’s a line I need to say to calm his anger.
“I’m innocent. There’s no way I’d be satisfied with something this trivial. I shouldn’t have let that bastard go so easily.”
That’s right. After all, I must make the Crimson Swine pay in the next loop as well. The Sage stands there dumbfounded, as if taken aback by this reply.
“So, the Spear Hero… no, does that mean I was mistaken…?”
